creators.name: Felix Beer
creators.bio: Researcher who works on decentralized governance where technology meets democracy, affiliated with the TUM Think Tank, Harvard Kennedy School and the BlockchainGov project, and a 2025 Summer of Protocols teaching fellow.
creators.why: Co-taught the 2025 Protocol School lectures on protocol art with Primavera De Filippi.
creators.bio_zh: 研究技术与民主交汇处的去中心化治理，任职或合作于 TUM Think Tank、哈佛肯尼迪学院和 BlockchainGov 项目，是 2025 年 Summer of Protocols 教学研究员。
creators.why_zh: 与 Primavera De Filippi 共同主讲 2025 年 Protocol School 的协议艺术课程。

creators.name: Peter Bauman
creators.bio: Editor in chief of Le Random, a digital-art collection and publication, who also writes under the name Monk Antony and interviews artists about protocol art and worldbuilding.
creators.why: Co-wrote with Primavera De Filippi a grammar of protocol art that sorts works by how they act as, with and about protocols and worlds.
creators.bio_zh: 数字艺术收藏与出版平台 Le Random 的主编，也以 Monk Antony 为笔名写作，常就协议艺术与世界构建采访艺术家。
creators.why_zh: 与 Primavera De Filippi 合写了一套协议艺术的“语法”，按作品是“作为”“借助”还是“关于”协议与世界来加以区分。

creators.name: Brian Droitcour
creators.bio: Art critic and editor-in-chief of Outland, an online magazine about art and digital technology.
creators.why: His essay 'Breaking Protocol' argues that the Ordinals protocol is itself an artwork, made by an artist for other artists and kept alive by collective inscription.
creators.bio_zh: 艺术评论家，曾任关注艺术与数字技术的线上杂志 Outland 的主编。
creators.why_zh: 他的文章《Breaking Protocol》认为 Ordinals 协议本身就是艺术作品：由一位艺术家为其他艺术家编写，并靠大家不断铭刻而存续。

creators.name: Shannon Jackson
creators.bio: Professor of Rhetoric and of Theater, Dance and Performance Studies at the University of California, Berkeley, who writes on social practice across performance and visual art.
creators.why: Her book Social Works reads participatory art through the systems of support (labor, maintenance, welfare, institutions) that every collective artwork depends on.
creators.bio_zh: 加州大学伯克利分校修辞学及戏剧、舞蹈与表演研究教授，研究横跨表演与视觉艺术的社会实践。
creators.why_zh: 她的《Social Works》从“支撑系统”（劳动、维护、福利与机构）来解读参与式艺术，指出每件集体作品都依赖这些支撑。

creators.name: Pablo Helguera
creators.bio: Artist, performer, writer and educator; director of adult and academic programs at the Museum of Modern Art in New York from 2007 to 2020.
creators.why: His handbook treats socially engaged art as a craft with methods, starting from how far participants take part in shaping a work.
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家、表演者、作家与教育者；2007 至 2020 年任纽约现代艺术博物馆成人与学术项目主任。
creators.why_zh: 他的手册把社会参与式艺术当作一门有方法的手艺来讲，从参与者在多大程度上参与塑造作品谈起。

creators.name: Tom Finkelpearl
creators.bio: American curator and former executive director of the Queens Museum, who served as New York City's Commissioner of Cultural Affairs from 2014 to 2019.
creators.why: What We Made gathers artists' own accounts of cooperative, co-authored art and proposes 'social cooperation' as the frame for understanding it.
creators.role_zh: 策展人、博物馆馆长与作者
creators.bio_zh: 美国策展人，曾任皇后区艺术博物馆执行馆长，2014 至 2019 年任纽约市文化事务专员。
creators.why_zh: 《What We Made》收集艺术家亲口讲述的合作与共同创作经验，并提出以“社会合作”作为理解这类艺术的框架。

creators.name: Max Haiven
creators.bio: Canadian writer, teacher, editor and organiser who studies money, financialization and the radical imagination; he also designs board games.
creators.why: Art after Money, Money after Art analyses how artists mock, sabotage, exit and hack money, with chapters on participation and on crypto economies.
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大作家、教师、编辑与组织者，研究货币、金融化与激进想象，也设计桌游。
creators.why_zh: 《Art after Money, Money after Art》分析艺术家如何嘲弄、破坏、退出和黑入货币体系，其中有专章讨论参与和加密经济。

creators.name: Geert Lovink
creators.bio: Dutch media theorist and critic of digital culture, founding director of the Institute of Network Cultures (INC) in Amsterdam, which publishes the MoneyLab readers.
creators.why: The MoneyLab Reader he co-edited collected early critical writing on crowdfunding, Bitcoin and alternative currencies by researchers and artists.
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰媒介理论家与数字文化批评者，阿姆斯特丹网络文化研究所（INC）的创始所长，该所出版 MoneyLab 系列读本。
creators.why_zh: 他参与主编的《MoneyLab Reader》汇集了研究者和艺术家对众筹、比特币与另类货币的早期批判性写作。

creators.name: Distributed Gallery
creators.bio: Collective of artists, carpenters and hackers that began in 2017 among friends exploring Ethereum; it made the Ready-Made Token, the Chaos Machine jukeboxes, the One Arm Crypto Bandit and the [aside] time-lock protocol.
creators.why: It explicitly calls its practice protocol art, treating each artwork as one situated experience of a larger set of rules that shapes how people interact.
creators.bio_zh: 由艺术家、木匠和黑客组成的团体，2017 年起源于一群探索以太坊的朋友；作品包括 Ready-Made Token、Chaos Machine 点唱机、One Arm Crypto Bandit 和时间锁协议 [aside]。
creators.why_zh: 他们明确把自己的实践称为协议艺术，把每件作品视为一套更大规则的一次具体体验，这套规则塑造人们如何互动。

creators.name: 0xfff
creators.bio: Pseudonymous artist and curator active in Ethereum art, who curated the contract show World Computer Sculpture Garden (2024).
creators.why: Curated an exhibition that is itself a smart contract with no closing date, whose state changes as visitors and artists act on it.
creators.bio_zh: 活跃于以太坊艺术领域的匿名艺术家与策展人，策划了合约展 World Computer Sculpture Garden（2024）。
creators.why_zh: 策划了一个本身就是智能合约、没有闭幕日期的展览，其状态随观众和艺术家的操作而改变。

creators.name: Protocol Institute
creators.bio: Organization launched in April 2026 to carry on the work of Summer of Protocols, with the magazine Protocolized as its flagship publication; Timber Stinson-Schroff is managing director and Venkatesh Rao director of research.
creators.why: It keeps the Summer of Protocols archive and lecture library, including De Filippi and Beer's lectures on protocol art, and publishes protocol fiction.
creators.bio_zh: 2026 年 4 月成立、接续 Summer of Protocols 工作的机构，以杂志 Protocolized 为旗舰出版物；Timber Stinson-Schroff 任执行主任，Venkatesh Rao 任研究主任。
creators.why_zh: 它保存 Summer of Protocols 的档案和讲座库（包括 De Filippi 与 Beer 的协议艺术课程），并出版协议小说。

works.title: Real Time Systems
works.description: Essay in Artforum (September 1969) that follows Systems Esthetics: Burnham describes the art world as an information-processing system and argues that artists should work with real-time information, events monitored and changed as they happen, rather than with finished objects.
works.description_zh: 1969 年 9 月发表于《Artforum》、接续《Systems Esthetics》的文章。Burnham 把艺术界描述为一个信息处理系统，主张艺术家应当处理“实时信息”，即在发生过程中被监测和改变的事件，而不是完成的物件。
works.idea_en: Treat the whole art system (critics, sales, contracts, visitors) as the software the artwork runs on.
works.idea_zh: 把整个艺术系统（评论、买卖、合同、观众）都当作作品运行其上的软件。
works.protocol: Burnham calls artists 'programs' supervised by the art world's 'metaprograms' and counts catalogues, reviews, sales and contracts as software extensions of the work; he singles out works whose outcome is set by live processes, such as Hans Haacke's planned real-time statistics of museum visitors and Les Levine's stock purchases presented as systems for producing art.
works.protocol_zh: Burnham 把艺术家称为受艺术界“元程序”监督的“程序”，并把图录、评论、买卖和合同都算作作品的软件延伸；他特别举出结果由实时过程决定的作品，例如 Hans Haacke 计划中的博物馆观众实时统计，以及 Les Levine 以“生产艺术的系统”名义进行的股票购买。
works.collective: The essay names audiences, markets and institutions as working parts of the artwork; it is read with Systems Esthetics as an early statement of art as a running system that depends on what other people do.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章把观众、市场和机构都列为作品的运作部件；它常与《Systems Esthetics》一起被阅读，被视为“艺术是依赖他人行动而运行的系统”这一观点的早期表述。

works.title: Behaviourist Art and the Cybernetic Vision
works.description: Two-part essay in the journal Cybernetica (1966–67) in which Ascott proposes a 'behaviourist' art: works designed as open systems that change through feedback with the people who use them, instead of fixed objects to be looked at.
works.description_zh: 分两期发表于期刊《Cybernetica》（1966–67）的文章。Ascott 提出一种“行为主义”艺术：作品被设计成开放系统，通过与使用者之间的反馈不断变化，而不是供人观看的固定物件。
works.idea_en: Design the work as a feedback loop: it is complete only when participants act on it and it responds.
works.idea_zh: 把作品设计成反馈回路：只有参与者对它采取行动、它又作出回应时，作品才算完成。
works.protocol: Ascott applies cybernetics to art: the artist sets up a structure and the rules by which it can change; spectators become participants whose actions feed back into the work, which keeps changing; the artist's task shifts from making a final object to designing the conditions for this exchange.
works.protocol_zh: Ascott 把控制论用于艺术：艺术家搭建一个结构以及它可以如何变化的规则；观众成为参与者，其行动反馈到作品中，使作品持续变化；艺术家的任务从制作最终物件转为设计这种交换得以发生的条件。
works.collective: The essay gave a theoretical base for participatory and networked work, including Ascott's own La Plissure du Texte (1983); it is reprinted as chapter 3 of Telematic Embrace (2003), the collection of his writings edited by Edward A. Shanken.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章为参与式与网络化创作提供了理论基础，其中包括 Ascott 自己的《La Plissure du Texte》（1983）；它作为第 3 章收入 Edward A. Shanken 编辑的 Ascott 文集《Telematic Embrace》（2003）。

paper.venue: Cybernetica 9, no. 4 (1966) and 10, no. 1 (1967); reprinted in Telematic Embrace (University of California Press, 2003)
paper.title: Behaviourist Art and the Cybernetic Vision

works.title: Protocol Art I and II (Protocol School lectures)
works.description: Two lectures given on 6 and 7 November 2025 for the Summer of Protocols Protocol School, in which De Filippi defines protocol art and tests the definition against cases from Sol LeWitt to Holly+ and her own Plantoid.
works.description_zh: 2025 年 11 月 6 日和 7 日为 Summer of Protocols 的 Protocol School 所做的两场讲座。De Filippi 给出协议艺术的定义，并用从 Sol LeWitt 到 Holly+ 以及她自己的 Plantoid 等案例来检验这一定义。
works.idea_en: Protocol art is allographic: the artist writes the rules and others make the instances with their own discretion.
works.idea_zh: 协议艺术是“异手”的：艺术家写下规则，由他人凭自己的判断做出一个个实例。
works.protocol: Part I separates autographic works, made by the artist's own hand, from allographic, protocol-based works whose rules others carry out with some discretion, citing Moholy-Nagy, LeWitt and Niele Toroni as precedents, and proposes axes for classifying them: atomic or systemic, strict or fluid, technical or social. Part II tests the boundary with audience cases (role-playing games, choreography, Xenakis scores, PostSecret, Pak's Merge and Censored) and studies Holly+ and Plantoid for distributed authorship, DAO governance and automated royalties.
works.protocol_zh: 第一讲区分“亲手”完成的作品与基于协议、由他人带着一定自主判断去执行规则的作品，以 Moholy-Nagy、LeWitt 和 Niele Toroni 为先例，并提出分类坐标：原子式或系统式、严格或灵活、技术性或社会性。第二讲用听众提出的案例（角色扮演游戏、编舞、Xenakis 的乐谱、PostSecret、Pak 的 Merge 与 Censored）检验边界，并以 Holly+ 和 Plantoid 分析分布式作者身份、DAO 治理与自动版税。
works.collective: Both sessions were seminars in which Protocol School participants brought cases and questions about discretion, copyright and when a protocol becomes generic; recordings and summaries are kept in the Protocol Institute's library.
works.collective_zh: 两场都是研讨形式，Protocol School 的参与者带来案例，并就自主判断空间、版权以及协议何时变得“通用化”等问题提问；录像和摘要保存在 Protocol Institute 的资料库中。

paper.venue: Protocol School 2025, Summer of Protocols / Protocol Institute (lectures)
paper.title: Protocol Art I and Protocol Art II

works.title: Living Aesthetics: A Grammar of Protocol Art and Worldbuilding
works.description: Essay published by Le Random on 24 August 2026 that maps protocol art as a grammar: it sorts protocols into instruction, automated, evolutionary and world protocols, and art into work made as, with and about protocols.
works.description_zh: Le Random 于 2026 年 8 月 24 日发表的文章，把协议艺术整理成一套“语法”：协议分为指令型、自动型、演化型和世界型，艺术分为“作为协议”“借助协议”和“关于协议”的作品。
works.idea_en: A protocol becomes a world when its rules describe whole environments rather than single things.
works.idea_zh: 当规则描述的不再是单个事物而是整个环境时，协议就成了一个世界。
works.protocol: The authors define a protocol loosely as a set of rules that produces an artifact. Read across, their diagram tracks how art loses and regains materiality; read down, it tracks how much control the artist keeps as rules pass from people (LeWitt, Fluxus, Yoko Ono's Grapefruit) to self-executing code, to systems with memory and metabolism (Plantoid, Botto, terra0) and to persistent worlds.
works.protocol_zh: 作者把协议宽泛地定义为“产出一件制品的一组规则”。他们的图表横向看，追踪艺术如何失去又重获物质性；纵向看，追踪当规则从由人执行（LeWitt、激浪派、小野洋子的《Grapefruit》）转向自动执行的代码、再到具有记忆与新陈代谢的系统（Plantoid、Botto、terra0）以及持续存在的世界时，艺术家还保有多少控制。
works.collective: The essay places works by many artists, from Alison Knowles and Félix González-Torres to Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst's Holly+ and the collective Keiken, on one map, and argues that art is moving back toward embodied experience through worlds.
works.collective_zh: 文章把许多艺术家的作品放在同一张图上，从 Alison Knowles、Félix González-Torres 到 Holly Herndon 与 Mat Dryhurst 的 Holly+ 以及团体 Keiken，并认为艺术正通过“世界”重新走向具身经验。

paper.title: Living Aesthetics: A Grammar of Protocol Art and Worldbuilding

works.title: Chaos Machine
works.description: Two linked wooden jukeboxes, each about 100 kg, that burn the banknote a visitor inserts, pay out ERC-20 tokens, and play a shared playlist stored on IPFS in sync on every connected machine.
works.description_zh: 两台相连的木制点唱机，每台约 100 公斤：观众投入的纸币被烧掉，换成 ERC-20 代币，所有联网机器同步播放一份存储在 IPFS 上的共享歌单。
works.idea_en: Burn state money to buy a voice in a shared, synchronized soundtrack.
works.idea_zh: 烧掉国家货币，换取在一段共享、同步的声音里发言的权利。
works.protocol: A visitor feeds a banknote into the machine; the note is burned and converted into ERC-20 tokens, which let the holder add a track to a collaborative IPFS playlist; the next song is chosen at random from a block hash and plays on all connected machines at once, and a printer issues a paper QR code.
works.protocol_zh: 观众把纸币投入机器；纸币被烧掉并换成 ERC-20 代币，持有者可以凭代币把一首曲目加入 IPFS 上的协作歌单；下一首歌由区块哈希随机选出，在所有联网机器上同时播放，打印机吐出一张纸质二维码。
works.collective: Machines stood at the Full Node workspace, at Kate Vass Galerie in Zurich and at Room77, Berlin's first bitcoin bar, and were shown in Simon Denny's exhibition Proof of Work at the Schinkel Pavillon; the playlist and the pile of burnt notes were made by the visitors who paid into it.
works.collective_zh: 机器曾放在 Full Node 工作空间、苏黎世的 Kate Vass Galerie 和柏林第一家比特币酒吧 Room77，并在 Simon Denny 于 Schinkel Pavillon 举办的展览“Proof of Work”中展出；歌单和那堆烧过的纸币都由付钱参与的观众共同造成。

paper.venue: Right Click Save, 21 May 2024 (interview by Georg Bak)
paper.title: The Aesthetic of a Protocol

works.title: [aside]
works.description: Protocol that makes an NFT on Ethereum non-transferable until a condition in the outside world is met; Chainlink oracles check data such as public sentiment, tides, moon phases or the ETH price, and unlock the work when the data match.
works.description_zh: 一个让以太坊上的 NFT 在外部世界满足某个条件之前无法转让的协议；Chainlink 预言机检查公众情绪、潮汐、月相或 ETH 价格等数据，数据一旦符合条件就解锁作品。
works.idea_en: Let the world outside the chain decide when an artwork may change hands.
works.idea_zh: 让链外的世界决定一件作品何时可以易手。
works.protocol: An artist or collector sets an unlocking condition for a token; Chainlink Functions query outside data sources through a decentralized oracle network, and the contract keeps the token locked until the returned data meet the condition. Twelve artists were invited to use it for the first releases.
works.protocol_zh: 艺术家或藏家为代币设定解锁条件；Chainlink Functions 通过去中心化预言机网络查询外部数据源，合约在返回的数据满足条件之前一直锁住代币。首批发行邀请了十二位艺术家使用这一协议。
works.collective: In the first release, AI Index by Obvious and Ivona Tau (27 May 2024), 100 NFTs are split into ten groups tied to ten intervals of an hourly X-based gauge of public sentiment about AI, so what the public posts decides which works become tradable. Other artists tied their works to moon phases and eclipses (Jared S. Tarbell), Thames tides (Anna Ridler), fog (Travess Smalley), earthquakes (Addie Wagenknecht) and the ETH price (Rhea Myers). ZKM Karlsruhe and Francisco Carolinum Linz received artist proofs of the releases.
works.collective_zh: 首批发行的《AI Index》由 Obvious 与 Ivona Tau 创作（2024 年 5 月 27 日），100 枚 NFT 分成十组，对应一个每小时更新、基于 X 平台的“公众对 AI 情绪”指数的十个区间，因此公众发布的内容决定哪些作品可以交易。其他艺术家把作品与月相和日月食（Jared S. Tarbell）、泰晤士河潮汐（Anna Ridler）、雾（Travess Smalley）、地震（Addie Wagenknecht）以及 ETH 价格（Rhea Myers）绑定。ZKM 卡尔斯鲁厄和林茨 Francisco Carolinum 获得了这些发行的艺术家版。

paper.venue: Verse Journal, 22 May 2024 (interview by Mimi Nguyen and Malte Rauch)
paper.title: Protocol Art, Museum Acquisitions, and Measuring Public Sentiment

works.title: World Computer Sculpture Garden
works.description: A 'contract show' that opened on Ethereum mainnet on 12 November 2024: the exhibition is itself a smart contract that lists seven contract artworks, and its website is generated from the contract's state, so it changes block by block and has no closing date.
works.description_zh: 2024 年 11 月 12 日在以太坊主网开幕的“合约展”：展览本身是一个智能合约，列出七件合约作品；网站由合约状态生成，因此逐个区块变化，没有闭幕日期。
works.idea_en: Treat the blockchain as a sculpture garden: open ground for long-running programs that anyone can visit and act on.
works.idea_zh: 把区块链当作雕塑公园：一片任何人都能来访并参与操作的、长期运行程序的开放场地。
works.protocol: Curator 0xfff deployed a show contract that points to the artists' contracts. Visitors act on each piece (adding words to 0xhaiku's poem, moving travellers along Figure31's road, toggling Rhea Myers' Is Art through Sarah Friend's Yesbot, posting a critique), artists can activate their pieces over time, and anyone may plant a flower in the guestbook by sending 0.01 ETH to the show contract.
works.protocol_zh: 策展人 0xfff 部署了一个指向各件作品合约的展览合约。观众可以操作每件作品（往 0xhaiku 的诗里添词、推动 Figure31 道路上的旅人前行、通过 Sarah Friend 的 Yesbot 切换 Rhea Myers 的 Is Art、发表一条评论），艺术家可以随时间激活自己的作品，任何人向展览合约发送 0.01 ETH 即可在留言簿里种下一朵花。
works.collective: The show's state is written by its visitors and artists: when the website was generated at block 26215368, the guestbook recorded 214 guests who had planted 301 flowers, and 59 travellers were on Figure31's road.
works.collective_zh: 展览的状态由观众和艺术家共同写入：网站在第 26215368 个区块生成时，留言簿记录了 214 位访客种下的 301 朵花，Figure31 的道路上有 59 位旅人。

works.title: Breaking Protocol
works.description: Editorial essay in Outland (22 May 2024) that opens an issue on Ordinals by arguing that the Ordinals protocol, launched by developer Casey Rodarmor in January 2023 to inscribe data on Bitcoin, is itself a work of art.
works.description_zh: 2024 年 5 月 22 日发表于 Outland 的社论文章，为一期 Ordinals 专题开篇。文章认为，开发者 Casey Rodarmor 于 2023 年 1 月推出、用于在比特币上铭刻数据的 Ordinals 协议本身就是一件艺术作品。
works.idea_en: A protocol written by an artist for other artists can itself be the artwork.
works.idea_zh: 一位艺术家写给其他艺术家使用的协议，本身就可以是作品。
works.protocol: Droitcour's argument: Ordinals marks inscribed segments of Bitcoin as special, but not all software recognizes the marking, so the protocol works only as long as people agree to treat inscriptions as art; it was developed by an artist for other artists, is maintained through the collective making of art and value, and acts as a 'parasitic twin' of Bitcoin.
works.protocol_zh: Droitcour 的论证是：Ordinals 把被铭刻的比特币片段标记为特殊，但并非所有软件都识别这种标记，所以协议只有在人们同意把铭文当作艺术时才成立；它由一位艺术家为其他艺术家开发，靠集体创作艺术与价值来维持，像比特币的“寄生双胞胎”。
works.collective: The essay frames an Outland issue guest-edited by the Ordinals artist FAR, and links the protocol to the longer history of 'Bitcoin graffiti' (jokes, poems and ASCII art written into blocks) traced by Kevin Buist. Outland's site has since gone offline; the text survives in the Internet Archive.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章为由 Ordinals 艺术家 FAR 客座编辑的 Outland 专题定调，并把该协议与 Kevin Buist 梳理的“比特币涂鸦”（写进区块的笑话、诗和 ASCII 艺术）的更长历史联系起来。Outland 网站现已下线，文本保存在互联网档案馆中。

works.title: Inventories, Not Identities
works.description: Essay published on 31 March 2021, the first in Kreutler's Gnosis Guild series on cryptonetworks and games, arguing that multi-signature accounts let online accounts belong to groups and hold collections of identities rather than one legal identity.
works.description_zh: 2021 年 3 月 31 日发表的文章，是 Kreutler 为 Gnosis Guild 撰写的加密网络与游戏系列的第一篇。文章认为，多签账户可以让在线账户属于一个群体，持有一组身份，而不是单一的法定身份。
works.idea_en: Make the account an inventory a group can share, not an identity one person must prove.
works.idea_zh: 让账户成为群体可以共享的“背包”，而不是一个人必须自证的身份。
works.protocol: A multi-signature account is controlled by several keys and executes a transaction only when a set number of them sign (2 of 3, 4 of 6); keys can themselves be other accounts, so cooperatives and DAOs can write their bylaws into the account and delegate votes, and a person can hold several pseudonymous identities in one inventory.
works.protocol_zh: 多签账户由多把密钥共同控制，只有达到规定数量的签名（三分之二、六分之四）才执行交易；密钥本身也可以是其他账户，因此合作社和 DAO 可以把章程写进账户并委托投票，个人也可以在一个“背包”里持有多个化名身份。
works.collective: The essay uses DAO treasuries such as the 4-of-6 multisig of the UNI Grants committee as examples of groups governing shared resources through such accounts; its sequel, A Prehistory of DAOs, followed in July 2021.
works.collective_zh: 文章以 DAO 金库为例，例如 UNI Grants 委员会的六分之四多签账户，说明群体如何通过这类账户管理共有资源；续篇《A Prehistory of DAOs》于 2021 年 7 月发表。

paper.venue: Gnosis Guild series, GnosisDAO on Medium, 2021
paper.title: Inventories, Not Identities: Why multisigs are the future of online accounts

works.title: Protocolized
works.description: Magazine of protocol fiction and essays launched by Summer of Protocols on 7 February 2025 with the issue 'Strange New Rules'; it reached issue #84 by the end of 2025 and since April 2026 is the flagship of the Protocol Institute, which keeps the Summer of Protocols archive as a library at protocolized.io.
works.description_zh: Summer of Protocols 于 2025 年 2 月 7 日以《Strange New Rules》一期创办的协议小说与评论杂志；到 2025 年底已出到第 84 期，2026 年 4 月起成为 Protocol Institute 的旗舰刊物，该机构把 Summer of Protocols 的档案整理为 protocolized.io 上的资料库。
works.idea_en: Use fiction to make the rules that run the world visible.
works.idea_zh: 用小说让运转世界的规则变得可见。
works.protocol: Each issue mixes stories, studies and columns about protocols; the magazine runs open writing contests for protocol fiction, in which 'strange rules' shape a story's world, and a special interest group that works out what the genre is.
works.protocol_zh: 每期刊登关于协议的小说、研究和专栏；杂志举办面向公众的协议小说征文比赛（由“奇怪的规则”塑造故事世界），并设有专门讨论这一文类的兴趣小组。
works.collective: Writers inside and outside the Summer of Protocols community supply the stories and contest entries; by October 2026 it had published more than 60 stories, announced a printed anthology, and launched Monstrous Times, a separate publication for 'strange rules' fiction.
works.collective_zh: Summer of Protocols 社群内外的作者提供小说和参赛作品；到 2026 年 10 月，杂志已刊发 60 多篇小说，宣布出版纸本选集，并另创专门刊登“奇怪规则”小说的刊物 Monstrous Times。

works.title: Social Works: Performing Art, Supporting Publics
works.description: Book (Routledge, 2011) that reads social practice across performance and visual art through the systems of support (labor, maintenance, welfare, institutions) that collective artworks depend on, with chapters on Mierle Laderman Ukeles, Rimini Protokoll, Elmgreen & Dragset and Paul Chan.
works.description_zh: Routledge 2011 年出版的书。作者从集体作品所依赖的支撑系统（劳动、维护、福利与机构）来解读横跨表演与视觉艺术的社会实践，设有讨论 Mierle Laderman Ukeles、Rimini Protokoll、Elmgreen & Dragset 和 Paul Chan 的章节。
works.idea_en: Every participatory work rests on systems of support; make them part of what you design.
works.idea_zh: 每件参与式作品都依靠一套支撑系统；把它们也纳入设计。
works.protocol: Jackson proposes to judge social works by how they stage and expose their supports (who maintains, who is paid, which institutions hold the event together) rather than by sorting them into 'autonomous' or 'social' art.
works.protocol_zh: Jackson 主张，评价社会性作品要看它们如何呈现并揭示自身的支撑（谁来维护、谁拿报酬、哪些机构把事件维系在一起），而不是把它们归入“自律”或“社会”艺术。
works.collective: Her cases are works made with sanitation workers, theatre ensembles, residents and audiences, such as Ukeles' maintenance art and Paul Chan's Waiting for Godot in New Orleans, read as models of shared, supported labor.
works.collective_zh: 书中的案例都是与环卫工人、剧团、居民和观众共同完成的作品，例如 Ukeles 的维护艺术和 Paul Chan 在新奥尔良上演的《等待戈多》，被视为共享且有支撑的劳动的范例。

paper.title: Social Works: Performing Art, Supporting Publics

works.title: Education for Socially Engaged Art: A Materials and Techniques Handbook
works.description: Short handbook (Jorge Pinto Books, 2011) that treats socially engaged art as a practice with its own methods, drawing on education, sociology and performance.
works.description_zh: Jorge Pinto Books 2011 年出版的小册子，把社会参与式艺术当作一种有自身方法的实践来讲，借鉴教育学、社会学和表演。
works.idea_en: Decide in advance how much the participants will shape the work: nominal, directed, creative or collaborative.
works.idea_zh: 事先决定参与者在多大程度上塑造作品：名义参与、指令参与、创造参与还是协作参与。
works.protocol: Helguera sorts participation into levels (nominal, directed, creative and collaborative) and gives artists working questions about community, time, conversation, antagonism and documentation when they plan a project with other people.
works.protocol_zh: Helguera 把参与分成几个层级（名义、指令、创造和协作），并为与他人共同规划项目的艺术家提供关于社群、时间、对话、对抗与记录的实用问题。
works.collective: Written from Helguera's work in museum education, the handbook is addressed to artists and educators who design projects with communities, and treats those communities as co-producers rather than audiences.
works.collective_zh: 这本手册源自 Helguera 在博物馆教育中的工作，写给与社群一起设计项目的艺术家和教育者，把社群视为共同生产者而不是观众。

paper.title: Education for Socially Engaged Art: A Materials and Techniques Handbook

works.title: What We Made: Conversations on Art and Social Cooperation
works.description: Book (Duke University Press, 2013) of fifteen conversations with artists and others about activist, participatory and co-authored art, which Finkelpearl frames as 'social cooperation'.
works.description_zh: 杜克大学出版社 2013 年出版的书，收录与艺术家等人的十五篇对谈，讨论行动主义、参与式和共同创作的艺术，Finkelpearl 以“社会合作”来概括这类实践。
works.idea_en: Judge cooperative art by the experience of everyone who made it, including its 'expert participants'.
works.idea_zh: 以所有共同创作者（包括“专家参与者”）的经验来评判合作式艺术。
works.protocol: Finkelpearl interviews artists such as Tania Bruguera, Rick Lowe, Mierle Laderman Ukeles, Harrell Fletcher and Lee Mingwei, critics Grant Kester and Claire Bishop, and the non-artist 'expert participants' who worked with them, and uses pragmatism as a critical frame for experience-based work.
works.protocol_zh: Finkelpearl 采访了 Tania Bruguera、Rick Lowe、Mierle Laderman Ukeles、Harrell Fletcher、李明维等艺术家，评论家 Grant Kester 和 Claire Bishop，以及与艺术家合作的非艺术家“专家参与者”，并以实用主义作为评判这类以经验为本的作品的批评框架。
works.collective: The conversations record how cooperation worked in projects with museums, libraries, neighbourhoods and online communities, and the book ends with a study of Rick Lowe's Project Row Houses in Houston.
works.collective_zh: 这些对谈记录了合作在与博物馆、图书馆、社区和网络社群共同开展的项目中如何运作；全书以对 Rick Lowe 在休斯敦的 Project Row Houses 的研究作结。

paper.title: What We Made: Conversations on Art and Social Cooperation

works.title: Art after Money, Money after Art: Creative Strategies Against Financialization
works.description: Book (Pluto Press, 2018) that studies contemporary artworks taking money as their subject, from cash, debt and credit to crypto, and sorts the strategies artists use to mock, sabotage, exit, decrypt and hack financialized capitalism.
works.description_zh: Pluto Press 2018 年出版的书，研究以货币为主题的当代艺术作品，从现金、债务、信用到加密货币，并梳理艺术家用来嘲弄、破坏、退出、解密和黑入金融化资本主义的策略。
works.idea_en: Artworks about money are experiments in imagining other systems of value.
works.idea_zh: 关于货币的艺术作品，是想象其他价值体系的实验。
works.protocol: Haiven groups artistic strategies into chapters on how money mediates life, on participation ('tactical parasitics and the encrypted common') and on encryption, and criticizes the hope that art can escape capitalism through crypto economies, arguing instead for an abolitionist horizon.
works.protocol_zh: Haiven 按章节归纳艺术策略：货币如何中介生活、参与（“战术寄生与加密的共有”）以及加密，并批评“艺术可以借加密经济逃离资本主义”的期望，转而主张一种废除主义的视野。
works.collective: It reads artist-made currencies, debt actions and participatory economies as tests of what money could be, and offers a critical counterweight to celebratory accounts of crypto art.
works.collective_zh: 书中把艺术家自制的货币、债务行动和参与式经济当作“货币还可能是什么”的试验来读，为对加密艺术的乐观叙述提供了批判性的平衡。

paper.title: Art after Money, Money after Art: Creative Strategies Against Financialization

works.title: MoneyLab Reader: An Intervention in Digital Economy
works.description: Reader (Institute of Network Cultures, 2015) edited by Geert Lovink, Nathaniel Tkacz and Patricia de Vries that maps experiments with crowdfunding, currency design, payment technologies and Bitcoin, with a foreword by Saskia Sassen.
works.description_zh: 网络文化研究所 2015 年出版的读本，由 Geert Lovink、Nathaniel Tkacz 和 Patricia de Vries 编辑，梳理众筹、货币设计、支付技术与比特币等实验，Saskia Sassen 作序。
works.idea_en: Money is a design space: artists, hackers and researchers can build and test alternatives.
works.idea_zh: 货币是一个设计空间：艺术家、黑客和研究者都可以建造并检验替代方案。
works.protocol: Under MoneyLab's call to democratize the design of financial futures, the reader asks of each new money system whether it is a genuine alternative or a creative extension of neoliberalism, and sets essays by economists and theorists beside artists' projects.
works.protocol_zh: 在 MoneyLab“让金融未来的设计民主化”的号召下，读本追问每一种新货币系统究竟是真正的替代方案，还是新自由主义的创意延伸，并把经济学家和理论家的文章与艺术家的项目放在一起。
works.collective: Thirty-four contributors wrote for it, among them Primavera De Filippi, Max Haiven, Paolo Cirio, Stephanie Rothenberg, Finn Brunton and Rachel O'Dwyer; it is free to download as INC Reader #10.
works.collective_zh: 共有 34 位作者参与，其中包括 Primavera De Filippi、Max Haiven、Paolo Cirio、Stephanie Rothenberg、Finn Brunton 和 Rachel O'Dwyer；该书作为 INC Reader 第 10 号可免费下载。

paper.venue: Institute of Network Cultures, Amsterdam, 2015 (INC Reader #10)
paper.title: MoneyLab Reader: An Intervention in Digital Economy
